newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down in lacklustre trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down in lacklustre trading.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B share index closed lower on Wednesday in lacklustre trading as investors turned away from the market to await fresh incentives, brokers said.
With the reporting season for 1997 interim results just underway, investors were waiting to see how individual companies fared before actively buying or selling, they said.
The B index fell 0.366 points or 0.47 percent to 76.966 points on volume of 8.780 million shares worth $4.353 million.
"The recent B share rebound was too sharp so there had to be some profit-taking," said an analyst at an Asian securities firm in Shanghai.
The B index also ended down slightly on Tuesday due to profit-taking after several days of gains, brokers said.
The recent strength of China plays listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange had also caused foreign investors to shift their attention away from Shanghai B shares, they said.
"B shares have also been influenced by the Hong Kong stock market, which has benefited from the Southeast Asia currency crisis," the analyst said.

Foreign investors had pulled their money out of Southeast Asian stock markets due to worries over local currencies, brokers said. That money had gone into Hong Kong, pushing up share prices in the former British colony and making that market look attractive, they said.
Of Shanghai's 45 B shares, 43 traded with 20 down, 15 unchanged and eight up.
Shanghai Sanmao Textiles Co Ltd was the biggest B share loser due to speculative selling. It fell $0.010 or 6.76 percent to $0.138.
Shanghai Narcissus Electric Appliances Industry Co was the second sharpest loser, falling $0.008 or 6.25 percent to $0.120.
Recently-listed Hainan Airlines Co was the most actively traded B share, ending the day unchanged at $0.542 on volume of around 1.7 million shares.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares fell as investors took profits and settled down to wait for fresh news, brokers said.
The A index closed down 9.809 points or 0.78 percent to 1,244.911 points on volume of 503.530 million shares worth 6.211 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 26.276 points or 0.68 percent to 3,844.676 points.
Brokers said the B share index could test lower on Thursday as investors waited for interim results, which companies will announce throughout July and August.
"Technically the market has ended its rebound and will test the downside in the short term," one local broker said.
